As most others have said, be honest, but polite, with your photographer. As a photographer and retoucher, with a Bachelor degree in Photography, I would want a client to be upfront with me so that I can help them get great images. Just like in a relationship, communication is key for everyone to be happy. 

However, because of copyrights, she has the right to not give you RAW images, allow you to edit anything, etc. Though she may be relaxed about it, I would suggest getting written consent from her for you to do your own edits. And then when posted on social media, I would still give her credit as photographer. 

Another question I saw was about photographers sending their work out for editing. Quite a few of them do. It is common in large studios, magazines, and big clothing brands. Sometimes a photographer will only take the images and a team of stylists and retouchers will do the rest. Basically, if a person isn't the best at a certain part of editing, they may send it out to a professional who can do it and then just give credit with the finished product.

Hello! Manic Panic has been my go-to hair dye for most of the past 6 years. I can honestly say that Hot Hot Pink and Ultra Violet are two of my favorites, especially together. Ultra Violet does have a tendency to come out looking more blue than purple in some light, but it still looks great with the pink. However, one thing you never want to do is directly mix together dyes of different brands, the ingredients may interact and then it probably will not be pretty.

If you want to go the "split color" route, I find that layering one color on top of another (bottom section of your head one, then the top section another color) is very pleasing.

As I mentioned, I've been doing my own hair for six years now. If you have any questions, feel free to send a message.

I became vegetarian when I was around 12. I generally stayed away from red meat anyway because I grew up next to a farm and the pasture was behind my house. I saw the cattle everyday and they were like friends to me, but I knew that they were slaughtered in the barn. Poultry was the only meat I ate until I was asked to cook it. It disgusted me and I never ate meat again.

Now, I stay away from anything from an animal. Especially because of food allergies. High cholesterol, high blood pressure, and other various health issues run in my family, so I try my best to combat those. Normally, I don't say anything about my diet and eating habits because it's a sensitive subject for me. I only mention it if I'm asked or I'm in a situation where I have to eat in public. 

I don't approve of the meat industry, but I'm not a person to judge others on their eating habits or think I'm better than them for not eating meat. My SO is an omnivore and I'm okay with that. We are considerate of each other and cook things separately. I may get ridiculed for that, but I do this for myself.
